description: This source file implements a server-sent events (SSE) endpoint for real-time attendance updates in a web application. It uses PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY for efficient event streaming and falls back to polling if necessary. The code manages SSE formatting, database channel listening, and streaming logic, exposing a Flask endpoint that streams attendance changes for a specified session.

classes.name: RealtimeAttendance
classes.description: Flask view class handling the SSE stream endpoint for real-time attendance updates associated with a specific session ID.

methods.name: str _format_sse(data: dict, event: str = "update", id: Optional[str] = None)
methods.description: Formats a dictionary of data as a Server-Sent Event string, including optional event type and ID, following SSE specifications.

methods.name: _pg_listen_cursor(channel: str)
methods.description: Context manager that opens a PostgreSQL raw connection to listen on a specified channel using LISTEN/NOTIFY, providing a cursor and connection, and ensuring cleanup.

methods.name: list[dict] _poll_attendance_changes(session_id: int, since_ts: Optional[str])
methods.description: Fetches recent attendance records for a given session, optionally filtered by a timestamp, returning a list of dictionaries representing each record.

methods.name: Iterable[str] _attendance_events_stream(session_id: int)
methods.description: Generator function that yields SSE-formatted strings for attendance changes, attempting to listen via PostgreSQL notifications and falling back to polling, with heartbeats to keep the connection alive.
